text: Put the thing you need tomorrow in front of the door tonight. Future you will trip over it, on purpose.
Set a timer for the boring task. It turns ‘forever’ into ‘until the beep’.
If a task takes less than 2 minutes, it’s a snack. Eat it now.
Write the very first step on a sticky note, not the whole task.
Lay out your clothes the night before. One less choice in the morning.
Keep a ‘landing pad’ by the door for keys, wallet and headphones. Always the same spot.
Music without words can make boring work feel lighter. Try one playlist just for tasks.
Stand up for a hard call or a hard email. A new position can wake up a new brain.
Can’t start? Make the task smaller until it feels almost silly.
Put your phone in another room for 20 minutes. Just 20.
Tell someone what you’ll do next. Saying it out loud makes it more real.
Half done is not failed. Half done is half done.
Lower the bar for ‘good enough’ today. Done beats perfect.
Keep a glass of water where you work. Sip, then go back.
When you open an app for one thing, say the thing out loud first.
Use a ‘parking lot’ note for random thoughts. Park them, don’t follow them.
Pair a dull task with something you like: a podcast, a snack, a sunny spot.
Before you leave, do a 3-point check: phone, keys, wallet.
Make the hard task the first thing you see when you open your laptop.
Clean one small area, not the whole room. One shelf counts.
Write the time you need to leave, not the time of the event. Leaving time is the real time.
Add 15 minutes to every ‘how long will this take?’ guess. Brains love to round down.
Bored of your system? Changing it is allowed. New can be fuel.
Take a 5-minute walk between two tasks. It’s a reset button for your head.
Keep a ‘done’ list, not just a to-do list. You do more than you think.
Open the document and type one ugly sentence. Ugly sentences can be fixed.
Hungry brains don’t focus. Eat something, then try again.
Rest is not a reward you earn. It’s part of the plan.
Pick your top 1 thing for the day. The rest is bonus.
Use a visual timer you can see. Time is easier to feel when it moves.
Set out your morning stuff right before bed, while you still remember.
Feeling stuck? Change rooms. Even the kitchen table can feel like a new start.
Big feelings pass faster when you name them. ‘I’m frustrated’ is a start.
Give boring tasks a silly name. ‘Laundry boss fight’ is more fun than ‘laundry’.
Turn off notifications you didn’t choose. Your attention is yours.
Text yourself the thing you just remembered. Right now, before it floats away.
Batch tiny errands: one trip, three stops.
A messy start is still a start.
Put recurring stuff (bills, birthdays) in your calendar once, so your head doesn’t carry it.
Work in short sprints with real breaks. Sprints beat marathons for busy brains.
If you forget why you walked into a room, go back to where you had the thought.
Keep spare chargers where you actually use them.
Say ‘let me check and get back to you’ before saying yes to new plans.
Do the task badly on purpose for 2 minutes. It often turns into doing it okay.
Hide what distracts you, show what helps you. Out of sight really is out of mind.
Plan for the version of you that’s tired, not the version that’s fired up.
End your work session by writing the next step. Starting tomorrow gets easier.
Some days are low-battery days. Pick low-battery tasks.
Hyperfocus is real. Set an alarm to check in: water, food, stretch.
Let the dishes soak. Soaking counts as starting.
Two-minute tidy before bed: just the stuff on the floor.
Use the same alarm sound only for leaving. Your brain will learn what it means.
Clear one notification badge at a time. Small wins add up.
Write tasks as actions: ‘email Sam about Friday’, not just ‘Sam’.
Comparing your inside to someone’s outside isn’t fair to you.
Body doubling helps many people: work next to a friend, even on a call.
When everything feels urgent, pick the one with the closest deadline.
Celebrate starting, not only finishing. Starting is the hard part.
Put a sticky note on your mirror for the one thing you can’t forget.
Keep a small ‘go bag’ with the basics, so leaving fast is easy.
If you’re spiraling, do one thing with your hands: wash a cup, fold a shirt.
Your brain isn’t broken. It just needs a different set of tools.
Gentle is faster than harsh. Talk to yourself like you’d talk to a friend.
Tomorrow is a fresh plate. Nothing carries over that you don’t want.
Wins from yesterday still count today.
Feeling frozen? Count backward from 5 and move on 1.
